subject: [RFC PATCH] mm/cma: don't release CMA pages still in use

reviews.author: Rik van Riel
reviews.summary: Posted a follow-up reply to address concerns raised by the reviewer. Mentioned that they will spin a v2 of the patch tomorrow and acknowledged that the hugetlb CMA code uses order 9 as the smallest size that may be returned to the CMA allocator.

2026-08-10.patch_summary: This RFC patch proposes a fix for a double-queue bug in the CMA (Contiguous Memory Allocator) code, which can lead to corruption of buddy lists and memory leaks. The patch introduces a new function __cma_release_frozen() that frees already-frozen pages in contiguous runs while skipping still-referenced pages. This change aims to prevent the CMA address space from being leaked when pages are still in use.
